chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Mehran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When death came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), he held me to his chest, then said: O my son, I advise you with what my father (peace be upon him) advised me when death came to him, and what he mentioned his father had advised him.
He said: O my son, beware of oppressing one who has no supporter against you except God.

key_terms.ظلم: Oppression, injustice, wrongdoing — a major sin in Islamic ethics
key_terms.ناصر: Supporter, helper, defender — one who aids the oppressed
key_terms.وصية: Testament, final counsel — advice given at the time of death, carrying immense weight in Islamic tradition

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin advise his son about oppression on his deathbed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) recounts the deathbed counsel of his father, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), who passed down a generational wasiyyah (testament) from Imam al-Husayn (AS): to never oppress someone who has no protector against you other than God. This hadith was narrated in a teaching assembly (majlis) of Shaykh al-Saduq in Muharram 368 AH, a month of particular reverence for remembering the Ahl al-Bayt and their sufferings.
